newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler profits jump 92 percent to record level.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler profits jump 92 percent to record level.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. Monday reported a 92 percent leap in profits for the third quarter as surging sales of its cars, trucks and minivans boosted its results to record levels.
The No. 3 automaker earned $680 million, or 93 cents a share, in the period, compared with profits of $354 million, or 45 cents a share, in the 1995 period.

"Chrysler's performance in the third quarter was outstanding," said Robert J. Eaton, chairman and chief executive officer. "It was fuelled by record setting demand for our products which led to a new third-quarter U.S. retail unit sales record and produced the best model year for U.S. retail unit sales in the company's history."
Revenues climbed to $14.4 billion for the quarter, a third-quarter record and an increase of $2.4 billion, or 20 percent, over third-quarter 1995 revenues of $12.0 billion.

The automaker said it shipped 650,529 units, compared with 581,853 in the year-ago period, boosting its share of the combined U.S. and Canadian retail car and truck market to 15.5 percent, from 13.6 percent in the third quarter of 1995.
In the international market, Chrysler's retail sales in the quarter were 57,209 vehicles, up 19 percent over the 48,207 vehicles it sold in the third quarter of 1995.
In Europe, Chrysler sold 28,079 vehicles, an increase of 28 percent over 21,918 vehicles in third-quarter 1995.

The automaker said it repurchased $452 million of its common stock in the latest quarter. The company initiated a $2 billion common stock buyback for 1996, and said it expects to repurchase an additional $1 billion of common stock in 1997.
Chrysler completed a $1 billion common stock buyback in 1995 and, through the first nine months of 1996, repurchased an additional $1.6 billion of common stock.
For the first nine months of 1996, Chrysler's net earnings were $2.722 billion, or $3.65 per share. That compared with $985 million, or $1.28 per share, for the first nine months of 1995.

Net earnings for the nine-month period included a $100 million charge for the write-down of Thrifty Rent-A-Car System, Inc., a $55 million charge for costs associated with a voluntary early retirement programme, and an $87 million gain related to the sale of its Electrospace Systems, Inc. and Chrysler Technologies Airborne Systems, Inc. units.

Net earnings for the first nine months of 1995 included charges of $162 million for production changes at Chrysler's Newark, Del., assembly plant, $96 million for the adoption of the consensus on Emerging Issues Task Force Issue 95-1, and $71 million to pay for minivan safety repairs.
Chrysler's stock ended Friday at $31.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
